You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test case `testOverrideVarianceWithMathClass` is setting the variance implementation in `SummaryStatistics` to a new `Variance` instance (with bias correction disabled, i.e. population variance). It then adds values and asserts that the computed variance matches the one directly evaluated by the `Variance` class on the same data array. The assertion fails, likely because the `SummaryStatistics` variance result differs from `Variance.evaluate`.

Looking at the `SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl` method, it simply assigns the new variance implementation instance after checking that the statistics are currently empty. This suggests that any new variance specification is accepted but doesn't do additional synchronization.

The `getVariance` method in `SummaryStatistics` delegates to `varianceImpl.getResult()`, so it queries the variance implementation’s stored result for the variance.

`getStandardDeviation` in `SummaryStatistics` returns the square root of variance when `n>1`. If variance is NaN, standard deviation would naturally be NaN.

Critically, `SummaryStatistics.addValue` increments several statistics implementations, including `varianceImpl.increment(value)` but only if `varianceImpl` is not an instance of the default `Variance`. In the test case's situation, `varianceImpl` is a `Variance` instance, so according to the code, `varianceImpl.increment(value)` is NOT called. This means the variance implementation we set is never updated with the data being added.

The `varianceImpl` field presumably remembers internal state and computes its result based on updates via `increment()` for individual values. Since overridden `varianceImpl` is never incremented, its internal state remains empty, returning NaN when queried for variance and standard deviation.

This explains why after setting `varianceImpl` explicitly to new `Variance(false)` and adding values, the variance and standard deviation computed through `SummaryStatistics` are NaN or incorrect. The statistics object fails to update the custom variance instance, so `getVariance()` returns an uninitialized calculation.

The root cause is: When overriding the variance implementation with a `Variance` instance, `SummaryStatistics.addValue()` fails to call `varianceImpl.increment(value)` because it skips increment on instances of `Variance`. Consequently, the internally stored variance statistics are not updated and `getVariance()` returns an invalid result (NaN), causing `getStandardDeviation` to also return NaN.

This issue specifically occurs because of the conditional skipping of the increment on the variance implementation if it is an instance of the default `Variance`. The failing test expects the variance implementation to be updated properly when overridden, but the code only updates `varianceImpl` if it is a non-`Variance` implementation, a contradiction.

Hence, overriding variance with a standard `Variance` instance leads to variance and standard deviation results of NaN due to lack of data updates in that variance instance.

No recent bug reports are clearly related and do not contradict this analysis.

Final note: The test calls `new Variance(false).evaluate(scores)`, which computes variance in a stateless manner (fresh evaluation from array), while `SummaryStatistics.getVariance()` depends on incremental updates which are missing for the overridden `Variance`.

This diagnostic fully explains the phenomenon in the bug report and test failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
